Friendly nudge — this has been open for a week with green checks and no review. The durable failure event only lands when `hasInterruptsOnly` misclassifies a mixed interrupt+failure cause, so the blast radius is small and contained; #49891 rides on the same branch and stays unaddressed until this lands. Glad to rebase or split the two fixes if that's easier to review.

I'll take this on v2. The desktop popover already badges non-command sources via `prompt.slash.badge.skill` / `prompt.slash.badge.mcp` / `prompt.slash.badge.custom`, so the data model knows the difference — the TUI slash list just doesn't surface it. On v2 the sources live in `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/slash-popover` (built-in registry vs. custom command/skill/MCP directories), so this is about threading the source kind into the row render and adding the same three badges.

Plan: tag each entry with its source at list-build time, render a badge column matching the desktop wording, and cover it in the slash-popover test with one entry per kind.

Fixes #51186

Still reproducing on the current v2 release line. Measured case from 2.0.15; the pattern survives the 26 September `v2` refactor.

**Measured case.** OpenCode 2.0.15, `packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts`, `compaction.keep.tokens: 16384`. An automatic compaction reduced context from approximately 107k to 82k tokens, but the checkpoint `recent` field retained 229,085 characters, roughly 57k tokens at characters / 4. The `findTailStart` logic is byte-identical at tag v2.0.18 (source-verified only; no runtime reproduction on that version).

- Unbounded rewind: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cd9a14a6b688d4021bee381dfd39d2cef9c0f862/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L349
- Retain-everything fallback: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/cd9a14a6b688d4021bee381dfd39d2cef9c0f862/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L361

**Case pattern.** The history handed to `findTailStart` is the transcript since the previous checkpoint. The budget walk picked a tail, then the unbounded `while` loop rewound its start to a user message. The previous compaction had fired mid assistant/tool sequence, so no user message existed after the previous checkpoint. With no anchor, the rewind reached the transcript start and the fallback retained everything since the previous checkpoint. Trigger: two automatic compactions during one long assistant/tool sequence with no user message in between.

**Reproduction status.** Replay of this exact checkpoint through the real request pipeline in an isolated standalone instance confirmed the oversized tail survives into the following model request. Replay verification only; no from-scratch reproduction of a new oversized checkpoint.

**Workaround.** A custom local plugin trims the checkpoint `recent` text in a context hook. It is deployed locally as mitigation. None of the core fix below is implemented, upstream or locally.

**Proposed fix.** Following this issue's budget invariant: keep the budget-selected boundary as the fallback. Rewind to a user message only when the resulting tail stays within `keep.tokens`; otherwise start at an assistant-step boundary. A v2 assistant message carries its own tool calls and results, so retaining whole messages keeps each step intact. Define an explicit policy for an individually oversized step instead of absorbing older steps. Note that the current `recentStart` on `v2` ([a64bc361](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/a64bc3616e9fa036e28ebf714a2b8a00138b3a78/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L714)) still retains everything when no user message exists since the previous checkpoint.

**Regression coverage.** User message within budget, distant user message, no user message since the previous checkpoint, consecutive automatic compactions, and an individually oversized assistant step.

Repro confirmed on `opencode v2.0.18` (Windows 11, TUI + Desktop 2.0.18, managed background service).

Spawns in `opencode.log`, all `role=server`:

- ~267x `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.EXE` (snapshot loop: `diff-files`, `ls-files`, `write-tree`) even while idle
- ~26x `C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.EXE` (one per `shell` tool call)

Sanitized sample:

timestamp=... message="spawning process" command="C:\\Program Files\\Git\\cmd\\git.EXE" args="[\"diff-files\",...]" cwd="<project-dir>" role=server
timestamp=... message="spawning process" command="C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.EXE" args="[\"-NoLogo\",\"-NoProfile\",...]" cwd="<project-dir>" role=server

Process layout when it flashes:

```text
opencode.exe serve --service   (detached, parent dead)
opencode.exe                   (TUI)
```

A/B on the same machine (spawns still logged in all three, only the visible window differs):

| mode | service process | flash? |
|---|---|---|
| managed `serve --service` (detached) | sibling of TUI, no console | yes |
| `opencode --standalone` (`serve --stdio`, child of TUI) | inherits TUI console | no |
| `serve --service` run visibly in a Windows Terminal tab, TUI + Desktop attached to it | has a real console | no |

How I tested the contender-side change: shallow-cloned branch `v2`, applied the one-line change to the service contender spawn, installed Bun 1.4.2 globally, ran `bun install`, then ran the dev CLI so it re-spawned its own service. Same spawns logged afterwards, visible windows persisted in my setup. The install was removed after the test.

Suggestion: both clean paths already exist in the product, so consider exposing one as a supported no-flash option — either document `--standalone` for single-client use, or surface a shared-service mode that runs attached to a visible console (what I do manually today: `serve --service` in a Windows Terminal tab, TUI + Desktop attached to the same service), so users don't have to choose between sharing one service and getting flashes.

@yveming bullet 2 says the backslash consumption is "independent of which bash binary is ultimately invoked". Worth settling, because if true then #51038 fixes only half of it. Three measurements of the same single argv element (`C:\Users\<name>\.cache\opencode\update-XXXX\install`, spawned directly, no shell in between, no quoting in play):

| bash that answered | result |
|---|---|
| Git Bash (`...\Git\usr\bin\bash.exe` and `...\Git\bin\bash.exe`) | exit 0, script runs; backslashes accepted |
| WSL via `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` | exit 127, `/bin/bash: C:Users\<name>...install: No such file or directory` |
| WSL via `...\WindowsApps\bash.exe` (@jpgomezv's machine) | exit 127, `/bin/bash: C:\Users\<name>\...install: No such file or directory` |

So the two wordings are produced by two different WSL entry points, not by a quoting layer sitting before bash, and in both WSL cases the script file is present (@jpgomezv verified before and after). A Windows path with backslashes is not itself a failure - which binary receives it is the whole difference. That is why #51038 selects the shell by asking each candidate its own `uname -s` and deliberately does no path rewriting: quoting the argument would still let WSL bash run the script, and then `install` reads `uname -s` as Linux and drops a Linux binary into the Windows install directory.

Your bullet 1 matches the shipped shape we read in `packages/cli/src/services/updater.ts` too, so the spawn being fixed is the same one.

Duplicate of #50236 — confirmed, same root symptom on 2.0.16.

Two details from my report that may be worth folding into the canonical issue, since they pin down the user-visible failure mode:

1. **The agent half is not cosmetic, it breaks prompts outright.** With the built-in `build` agent disabled (a normal thing to do when you want your own primary agent to be the only one), every `session/prompt` never returns — no completion and no error — and the server log shows `Failed to drain Session: Session.AgentNotFoundError: Agent not found: "build"` at `SessionRunner.prepareContext`. For an ACP client this presents as "the bot answers its own messages but never replies", with no diagnostic on the client side.

2. **Clean A/B on 2.0.16, same directory and same config.** `opencode run "say hi"` → `> yolo · space-bunny-free` (configured `default_agent` and `model` both honored). Same directory over `opencode acp` → `mode current=build values=['build', 'plan']`, `yolo` never offered, and the `model` option replaced by the newest available model from a different provider.

Repro driver, verbatim log lines, and the stdlib-only Python ACP probe are in the issue body until this is closed.
Closing as a duplicate of #50236.

Adding a failure mode that the timeout theory in this thread does not cover, because it isn't a timeout at all.

@aron-intframe's code-level read is right — `Effect.forEach(..., { concurrency: "unbounded" })` with a per-server `mcp.timeout ?? 30_000` means no shared budget, and N dials expiring on one constant explains "12 servers failing in the same second". I agree with that.

But the synthetic servers used there (`python` shims) don't install anything on spawn. Servers configured the way opencode's own docs recommend do:

```jsonc
{
  "type": "local",
  // Or ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command"]
  "command": ["npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"]
}
```

`bunx` / `npx` install-then-run on **every** spawn. Under unbounded concurrency those installs collide in the shared cache, the losers exit during startup, and the server never reaches `initialize` — so it surfaces as `Connection closed`, not `Operation timed out after 30000ms`. Different symptom, same trigger.

## Reproducible without opencode

8 concurrent invocations of the exact `command` array, 3 rounds:

```sh
for round in 1 2 3; do
  for i in $(seq 1 8); do
    (bunx --bun some-mcp-pkg@latest </dev/null >/dev/null 2>err_${round}_$i; echo "r$round-$i=$?" >>res) &
  done
  wait
done
```

**11 of 24 invocations failed (46%).** Child stderr:

```
FileNotFound: failed copying files from cache to destination for package zod
FileNotFound: failed copying files from cache to destination for package @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
FileNotFound: failed copying files from cache to destination for package hono
error: Failed to link which: EEXIST
```

At 4-way concurrency it was ~2/4; at 8-way, 11/24. Single invocation never fails.

## Why this matters for the proposed fix

A warm-up / pre-spawn mechanism is the right shape, but pre-spawning with the same `command` doesn't help by itself — N concurrent `bunx` still race. The install has to be serialized (or done once up front and the spawn pointed at the installed binary) for warm-up to actually close this.

Two related details that constrain the design:

- **Pinning the version makes it worse, not better.** `some-mcp-pkg@2.0.0` makes bun resolve the full tree (135 packages instead of 2), and then *all* parallel invocations fail with `EEXIST`. The floating tag happens to keep the install shallow.
- **Per-directory spawns multiply the window.** `ps` under a single server PID showed 6-7 identical processes per server, each with its own `/tmp/bunx-1000-*` install — so 7 installs race instead of 1. This is the leak in #51003 / #51249, but it's also an amplifier here.

Also worth noting for diagnosis: opencode discards the child's stderr and reports only `Connection closed`, so the `EEXIST` never surfaces. The timeout theory led me (and probably others) to look at slowness rather than at the install.

Environment: opencode 2.0.16, Ubuntu 24.04, bun 1.3.5, node v24.6.0, GNOME Terminal / X11.

Confirming this on **2.0.16** (reported here on 1.18.30), plus two failure shapes that the npm-spec path can produce which aren't covered above — both with a package that installs perfectly cleanly.

## 1. A subpath export in `package` is parsed as a version

`opencode-pty`'s own README documents this for OpenCode V2:

```jsonc
"plugin": [ { "package": "opencode-pty/v2", "options": { ... } } ]
```

That does not work. The `package` field is resolved as `name@version`, so `opencode-pty/v2` becomes a request for `opencode-pty@v2`, which 404s (the package has only `0.0.0 … 0.4.0`) and falls back to git:

```
WARN message="failed to load plugin" target=opencode-pty/v2
  cause="Cause([Fail(NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: An unknown git error occurred))])"
```

So a plugin that documents the `pkg/subpath` syntax for opencode 2.x cannot be loaded through the `package` field at all. The subpath exists in `exports` (`"./v2"`) — it just isn't reachable this way.

## 2. A valid install can still be unloadable

Pinning to a real version installs fine but resolves the **v1** entry (`dist/index.js`), which opencode 2.x rejects:

```
INFO msg="loading plugin" id=opencode-pty@0.4.0
     entrypoint=file:///~/.cache/opencode/npm/opencode-pty@0.4.0/.../dist/index.js
WARN message="failed to load plugin" target=opencode-pty@0.4.0
  cause="Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function.
         (cause: SchemaError(Missing key at ["default"]))"
```

The install is valid and the module imports fine under Node 24 — but only `./dist/src/v2/index.js` exports the `{ id, setup }` shape 2.x requires. So "the install succeeded" is not sufficient evidence that the npm-spec path worked, which may be why this looks like a silent no-op.

## 3. `file://` must point at a directory, not a file

The workaround above works, but the direct form does not — pointing `package` straight at the entry file:

```jsonc
"package": "file:///.../opencode-pty/dist/src/v2/index.js"
```

```
WARN message="configured plugin path must be a directory"
     target=/.../opencode-pty/dist/src/v2/index.js
```

Only a directory is accepted, so a local re-export file is required, not a direct file URL. Two further details if anyone tries the bare-specifier form (`export { default } from "opencode-pty/dist/src/v2/index.js"` from a local plugin file): the package must be a real dependency of the config dir (`~/.config/opencode`), and the import has to be a **relative path** — a bare specifier failed with `Cannot find package 'opencode-pty' imported from ...` even though it was present in `~/.config/opencode/node_modules`.

What did work: `bun add`/`npm install` into `~/.config/opencode`, then a one-line re-export in `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` using a relative path. No plugin-related log lines after that.

Environment: opencode 2.0.16, Ubuntu 24.04, bun 1.3.5, node v24.6.0. Happy to provide the full log excerpts if useful.

Adding a data point that may explain why this looks like a v2 login requirement, since that is the conclusion the behavior invites — it is not one.

On 2.0.16, with **no** Zen credential anywhere (no `OPENCODE_API_KEY` in the environment, nothing Zen-related in `opencode auth list`, global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` containing only `$schema`):

- `opencode run -m opencode/space-bunny-free "say hi"` in a project directory → answers normally, as `> <agent> · space-bunny-free`.
- `opencode acp` in that same directory → the `model` session option contains **zero** `opencode/*` entries, and a new session comes up on the "newest available supported model" from an unrelated provider instead.

So the free Zen models are reachable without any credential (they also answer a plain `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions` with no `Authorization` header), but the ACP catalog never lists them.

Setting `OPENCODE_API_KEY` to a dummy value makes the `opencode/*` and `opencode-go/*` entries appear in the catalog and the configured `model` pin get honored — `session/new` then reports `currentModelId=opencode-go/space-bunny-free` — but every prompt fails with:

```text
{"code":-32000,"message":"Authentication required: provider authentication required"}
```

even though that same model is the one that just worked unauthenticated over plain HTTP. That points at a client-side credential gate in the catalog/availability path rather than at anything the endpoint requires.

Asking for either of these would make the failure much easier to act on:

1. treat a provider as available when the model is actually reachable, not only when a credential is stored (or let the catalog include keyless-reachable free models), and
2. when a configured `model` is dropped for a fallback, say why in the session result or a log line, so a working pin failing to apply does not look like a policy change.

I ended up cancelling this and resolving it on my end. Here is the explanation for future readers as I see a lot of activity here still

In opencode v2 every terminal call is made in a new child process terminal window

> Small update from my side: we already have this working in OpenCode 2 with our local plugin `opencode2-subagent-aux`. We used it in many sessions with real tasks, and it works well for us. Thank you, V2 plugin API was enough for this :)
> 
> [@opencode-agent](https://github.com/opencode-agent), we followed the plugin direction you suggested, but a little differently. We extend the existing `subagent` tool with `ctx.tool.transform`, instead of creating child sessions ourselves. So native OpenCode still handles parent links, foreground/background, cancellation, permissions and completion notifications.
> 
> We added three optional parameters: `directory`, `model` and `effort` (model variant). They also work with `sessionID`: we can continue the same child, move it to another directory and change its model/effort. History stays with the session. Without these parameters, it works as usual.
> 
> The main trick: native `subagent` waits for its `progress` callback after the child is ready, but before sending the prompt. We apply our changes there. Short version of this part, with validation and error handling left out:
> 
> // directory and selection are already resolved and validated.
> let applied = false
> 
> return yield* native.execute(nativeInput, {
>   ...context,
>   progress: Effect.fn(function* (update) {
>     if (!applied && update.status === "running" && update.sessionID) {
>       const child = yield* runtime.session(update.sessionID)
>       if (directory && child.location.directory !== directory) {
>         yield* runtime.move(child.id, directory, child.location.workspaceID)
>         yield* awaitDirectory(directory, () =>
>           runtime.session(child.id).pipe(
>             Effect.map((s) => s.location.directory),
>           ),
>         )
>       }
>       if (selection) yield* runtime.switchModel(child.id, selection)
>       applied = true
>     }
>     yield* context.progress(update)
>   }),
> })
> Here `runtime` wraps `ctx.session.get`, `ctx.session.move` and `ctx.session.switchModel`. We wait for the actual directory change because `move` only queues it.
> 
> We also tested that the first child request gets local `AGENTS.md`, skills and agent settings, and relative file reads work in the target directory.
> 
> Of course, this depends on the current order of `progress` before `prompt`, so it needs checking when OpenCode changes. But for our original use case, it is solved now. No need to reopen from my side. Thanks again!

Additional evidence: it is not only that math is not typeset — the Markdown renderer also
**corrupts the LaTeX source**, so the user cannot even read the raw formula correctly.

Sent as a standalone message:

```
$$p'_{161} = p_{161} + A\,(p_{161} - p_{161}) = p_{161}$$
```

Displayed in the desktop app (v2.0.12) as literal text:

```
$$p'{161} = p{161} + A,(p_{161} - p_{161}) = p_{161}$$
```

Two changes are visible, both explained by CommonMark/GFM parsing rather than math parsing:

- `p'_{161}` → `p'{161}`: the first two `_` are paired as emphasis and consumed, so the
  underscores disappear. The remaining `_` are intraword (preceded by a letter) and stay.
- `A\,(...)` → `A,(...)`: the backslash escapes ASCII punctuation, so `\,` renders as `,`.

This happens for a standalone message too, not only when the formula is mixed with prose.
Inside a fenced code block the source is preserved verbatim, but it is still not typeset.

Repro (desktop, Windows 11, v2.0.12):

1. Send a message that contains `$$p'_{161} = p_{161} + A\,(p_{161} - p_{161}) = p_{161}$$`.
2. Observe the rendered message: delimiters shown literally, `_` eaten as emphasis, `\,` reduced to `,`.

Expected: either typeset math, or at minimum no silent corruption of the source. Rendering
math (KaTeX/MathJax) would fix both, but it may also be worth ensuring that math delimiters
and their contents are excluded from emphasis/escape processing.

I looked into this on `v2` and can reproduce the cause: this is a regression from the redefinition of `connected()`.

On `dev`, `useConnected()` reports whether a provider is configured (`packages/tui/src/component/use-connected.tsx`). On `v2` it delegates to `hasConnectedProvider`, i.e. "some integration has connections" (`packages/tui/src/util/connected-provider.ts`: `integrations.some((integration) => integration.connections.length > 0)`).

The model dialog carried the old gates over verbatim, so with no integration connected:
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-model.tsx:160` hides the `model.dialog.favorite` action (`hidden: !connected()`)
- `dialog-model.tsx:32` drops the favorites list, and `:27`/`:31` gate the Favorites and Recents sections through `showExtra`
- `dialog-model.tsx:102` also feeds `connected()` into the option set

The missing hint and the dead toggle are the same cause: `packages/tui/src/ui/dialog-select.tsx` builds its keymap from `shownActions()` (`:156` filters `!item.hidden`, `:162` registers from it), so a hidden action is not just invisible, its keybinding is never registered and `ctrl+f` does nothing at all.

Your follow-up comment matches exactly: favorites and their hint returned as soon as an integration was connected again. Local favorites and recents are client-side preference state, so gating them on integration connectivity looks unintended; only the integration-facing entry (`model.dialog.provider`, title at `:147`) should depend on it.

I would like to work on this. Plan: stop gating the favorites list, the Favorites/Recents sections and the `model.dialog.favorite` action on integration connectivity, keep the gate for the integration entry, and add a dialog test covering the no-integration case.

Confirming this is not a one-off gateway quirk — the same silent-truncation class shows up through a subagent-delegation layer rather than a direct session, where the failure shape is worse than a lost output.

What we observe on our side:

- A child that burns its whole output budget inside the reasoning channel finishes with `status: completed` and an **empty** payload. No error, no partial output, nothing to retry from.
- The stored message carries `finish: "length"` and **no** error object, so every consumer that keys off task status sees a clean success.
- Practically, this becomes a silent-correctness failure rather than a lost-output one: documented in anomalyco/opencode#38866, a downstream model "almost treated the empty result as a valid no-findings critique" instead of re-dispatching. As a mitigation while the core fix lands, we treat a completed-but-empty child result as a failure signal and re-dispatch — task status alone is not trustworthy for orchestrated work.

On anomalyco/opencode#40142 the chosen split looks right, and the bounded-one-continuation design answers the "stay an error or become a recoverable stop reason" question. Two things it does not cover, in case they are worth tracking alongside:

1. **The aborted-stream case has no equivalent recovery.** A dropped provider stream is recorded as `finish: "unknown"` with zero usage and no text (anomalyco/opencode#37852). Its retry fix (anomalyco/opencode#39473) was closed without merging, so a dropped stream is still surfaced as an empty result rather than a retry — and this is the mode that produced the silent-correctness failure above. If the entry-gate plus in-loop exclusion pattern generalises to `"unknown"`, that gap may close in the same change family.

2. **A third mode is separate, and a `length`-only special case will not cover it.** Premature termination well under any limit — status `completed`, output far below the ceiling (anomalyco/opencode#32132). That one explicitly is not truncation.

Related but outside this repo: a downstream orchestrator amplifies both cases by bypassing its own output-size clamp on synchronous delegated results, and by polling an already-dead child for the full inactivity window — so one truncated turn costs a full wait cycle before it is noticed.

Not filing a separate issue; anomalyco/opencode#40146 plus anomalyco/opencode#40142 already cover the core.

Thanks for this — the `eq(SessionTable.path, input.subpath)` trace at `store.ts:108` and the `NULL = ''` SQL point both check out on my install.

One correction to the **scope**, from a much larger dataset (opencode 2.0.18, upgraded from 1.18.x; 4,364 rows in `session_v2` across 43 projects):

The `NULL = ''` case is real, but it's the smaller half. `eq(path, '')` also excludes every row whose path is a real subdirectory, because `'sub/dir' != ''`. Measured over top-level sessions in `session_v2`:

| `path` state | count | reachable via the project picker |
|---|---|---|
| `path = ''` | 16 | yes |
| `path IS NULL` | 34 | no |
| `path = '<subdir>'` | 197 | no |

So **231 of 247** top-level sessions are unreachable through the picker, and only **34** of those are the `NULL` case. About **85%** of the hidden rows are hidden simply because the filter demands `''` while their path is an actual directory.

I'd argue this is one defect rather than two. The client sends `subpath: ''` unconditionally — `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-session-list.tsx:70` on `v2`:

```ts
subpath: path.relative(current.project.directory, current.directory).replaceAll("\\", "/"),
```

`path.relative()` returns `""` when the active directory is the project root, which is the common case. That `""` then becomes an equality filter. The `NULL` semantics you describe are the same filter, just meeting rows whose path happens to be `NULL` instead of rows whose path is a directory.

The fix is one line, on the client, and it cures both halves at once:

```ts
const subpath = path.relative(current.project.directory, current.directory).replaceAll("\\", "/")
// ...
{ project: current.project.id, ...(subpath ? { subpath } : {}) }
```

A genuine subdirectory still filters, exactly as before.

One caveat on scope: the server guard should stay `!== undefined`. `path = ''` **legitimately** means "a session started at the project root" — `Session.create` derives it from `path.relative(project.directory, location.directory)`, which is `""` when the two match — so relaxing it server-side would remove the ability to filter for root-level sessions.

Two things that may be useful for reproducing:

- The panel's search box is hit by the same filter, because search reuses this request and only adds `search` to it. A session that provably exists returns nothing when you type its title.
- A minimal repro that needs no database state at all: compare
  `GET /api/session?limit=50&order=desc&parentID=null&project=<ID>&subpath=`
  against the same URL with `subpath` omitted.

I have this on a branch with regression tests (asserting the parameter is absent at a project root and present in a subdirectory; the root case fails against unfixed `v2`). Posting the measurement first since it substantially widens the reported scope — I'll open a PR against `v2` after this.
